source_title: Producer Price Index News Release - 2026 M06 Results

values.metric: Final demand less foods, energy, and trade services

values.note: Gasoline prices -12.0%; nearly two-thirds of the goods decline traced to gasoline

revisions: BLS states that some February through May figures were revised because late reports and respondent corrections became available. The release does not summarize every old-versus-new value in prose, so no unverified revision delta is supplied here.
methodology_changes: Effective with June 2026 data, BLS incorporated data for 22 resampled industries classified under the 2022 NAICS.

analysis.headline: U.S. final-demand PPI fell 0.3% in June, but the decline was concentrated in energy and goods while services and the core measure still rose.
changes: Final-demand PPI shifted from +0.6% in May to -0.3% in June, seasonally adjusted.
Final-demand goods fell 1.4%, led by a 6.4% energy decline; final-demand services rose 0.2%.
The measure excluding foods, energy, and trade services slowed from +0.8% in May to +0.1% in June; its 12-month increase was 5.1%.
analysis.behavioral_readout: The combination is more consistent with a sharp easing in volatile goods and energy pricing than with broad producer-price deflation: gasoline and energy pulled the headline down, while service prices and the core measure continued to rise.
implications: Inference: headline pipeline price pressure eased in June, but persistent services and core increases limit the evidence for broad disinflation.
alternative_explanations: Energy-price volatility can reverse quickly and may dominate the one-month headline.
Monthly revisions and the June industry resampling can affect comparisons for detailed components.

caveats: The monthly figure is seasonally adjusted, while the 12-month figure is unadjusted.
This is the first local baseline for this dataset; exact February-May revision deltas were not reconstructed without prior local records.
